You are now immersed amidst a vast green cloud of tangled vegetation. Advance
becomes arduous, yet not impossible, as the weeds stick to you, and you can only
set the thick blades aside with great difficulty. As you step onwards, the space
you leave disappears as the immense mass of grass fills it, closing
suffocatingly around you, reducing your vision to a few paces, and threatening
to engulf you.
name: Surrounded by the High Grass

desc:
A thick layer of weeds have taken possession of what once was cultivated ground.
Beneath the scrub, you can still catch a glimpse of the brown earth, and even
figure out the lines of the furrows. The grass crowds around the plots, but only
tufts and bushes grow inside them, thus making them look like unyielding
bastions in the middle of the infinity of the grasslands.
name: Abandoned Field

desc:
Although the soft swinging of the fresh, deep-green grassy stems gives them a
fragile, delicate look, reality is way different. Winters are extremely tough
and cold, frosts are common, and dew greets the sun every dawn as it rises over
the shadowy Mirkwood forest. Summers, on the contrary, are really hot, almost
torrid. Moreover, most of the animals depend on the juicy grass for their
survival. Thus, behind their weak appearance, the sprigs grow strong and
fibrous, with sharp edges and mighty, firm roots. From the most robust beorning
to the smallest grasshopper, every inhabitant of these lands knows how tough
life is over here.
name: Wild Plains

desc:
Some miles northwards, the top of a low hill rises heavily over the grasslands,
its wide green slopes spreading all around, as if the hill had been wildly
smashed by the hammer of a giant, or perhaps scattered under the march of a huge
army. Here the hillsides incline shyly, almost imperceptibly, as if reluctant to
leave the broad prairie. Only near the top do the slopes become slightly
steeper.
name: At the Foot of a Green Hill

desc:
A high and impenetrable hedge delimits this large farmhouse, whose only way in
is apparently the broad wooden gate that breaks the hedge directly to the west.
The ground seems to descend slightly southeastwards, where there stand a number
of outbuildings and a long house a bit further. A shapely, wide, grassy track
starts at the gate and sets out towards there, going down the meadow, which
appears to be mostly covered with gardens full of lively- coloured flowers, and
dotted with a few old oaks here and there.
name: Inside the Farmstead

desc:
A bend in the high hedge that surrounds this great farmhouse suggests that you
are now at its northwestern corner. The thorny wall towers quite high over a
man's head. Small, dark leaves with pointed spikes along their edges, and what
seem twisted stems with prickles all over, intertwine so densely that no little
bit of light can get through the tangled barrier. In contrast with it, the vivid
garden, that shines in a deep green background sprinkled with the many loud
colours of the flowers, extends to the very foot of the wall, as if totally
unaware of it.
name: Gardens by the Hedge

desc:
Tens and tens, or perhaps hundreds of huge beehives disposed in rows fill this
part of the farmstead. They all seem exactly the same, with their golden
bell-shaped tops made of straw. A deafening noise fills the air, due to the
unceasing drone of the very many bees. And such bees! For their bulky size and
extremely intense colours, it is clear that they are uncommon specimens, but
they are not less hard-working because of that, and so they do their utmost to
produce honey and wax for their master.
name: The Giant Beehives

desc:
This wide path goes down through the hillside, across the green spreads and the
flower patches, heading towards a group of small wooden buildings in the south,
and, beyond them, down into a small courtyard in front of a low, long, wooden
house. In the other direction, it bends softly westwards, leading to the broad
gate in the hedge, but not entering the beehive fields that lie to the north,
from where you can hear a loud noise. Animals seem to wander freely through
pastures and gardens, but always alert to the presence of foreigners.
name: A Track through the Gardens

desc:
This little long building always seems fresh and in the shade. The light that
comes in through the entrance hole is not enough to illuminate but the first few
steps inside. Everything seems extraordinarily clean. There are large piles of
straw, as golden as the sun, shining out in the dim light. Leaning against the
side wall is a long watering trough, filled with clear, almost crystalline
water. Beside it, lay several brushes and buckets. And despite their obvious
residence here, the smell of the animals is remarkably faint.
name: Beorn's Stables

desc:
The track runs across a group of several wooden buildings of different sizes.
There are granaries, sheds and barns, and a few others whose purposes are not
clear, and they all have walls made of thick, rough, oaken logs, and most of
them are thatched-roofed, but some have wooden roofs instead. A great oak-wood
extended all over this place way back, but a large part of it has been felled,
and only the wide belt that surrounds the farmstead, and a few huge and lonely
ancient trees, that grow scattered inside, are still standing. These few trees
cast ample shadows, in which the animals can lie on the grass to rest.
name: Path through Some Outbuildings

desc:
Located in front of the entrance to the long, U-shaped wooden house, the sides
of this little courtyard are enclosed by the house wings, as its back side is by
the front wall, where a small and dark door opens into the house. In the middle,
there is a great oak trunk that shows evident signs of axe hacks. A number of
lopped branches pile up in disorder beside it. To the north, a grassy track goes
through the outbuildings, before continuing off into the distance.
name: The Courtyard

desc:
A large hearth occupies the middle of this spacious, long hall, and it remains
lit throughout the whole year, filling the room with the crackling of logs, the
smell of burning wood, and the warmth of its fire. The smoke climbs lazily in
search of the way out through an opening in the ceiling, past the heavy
blackened rafters. Two rows of thick pillars, with what appear to be brackets
for torches, support the roof that, like the walls and the floor, is made of
wood. Slightly raised platforms run along both side walls, that are abutted by
the wings, and so have no windows. Thus, the room is only dimly lit. On the
north, a dark door leads outside, and so does a smaller one in the rear wall.
name: Beorn's Hall

desc:
Running through the wide gardens, this narrow little path heads northwards,
parallel to the western wing of the house. Its outer wall is low and has no
windows, and it is made of large, circular, hardly-worked trunks. Similarly, the
roof ascends steeply towards the peak, right along the middle of the house.
Flowers crowd around the track, and they seem to have been deliberately planted
to grow facing it, offering their colour to whoever follows the way.
name: The Garden Path

desc:
These wide gardens, crammed with colour and liveliness, spread over most of the
southern area of the farmhouse. A great assortment of flowers and plants are
here, and some of them are so extremely rare that they may not be found anywhere
else. Some have big crowns of silky petals; others are small and
handbell-shaped; a few seem long and swaying; the variety is endless. And they
shine in the most variegated colours, in deep and pale shades, and dark and
light hues, like a great rainbow over the ground, but one with its stripes mixed
and intermingled in a myriad of coloured blotches.
name: Flowered Gardens

desc:
A carpet of thick dust covers all the surfaces, as everywhere else in the hole,
but here it seems dotted with small black stains and filth of dubious source.
The walls show dark marks of damp, and so does the ceiling, flat near the door
but inclined in the rear end. A round dormer window leads outside there,
although the dense vegetation conceals it partially. A wide stain spreads
beneath it, exuding a piercing moisture smell. A broad bed, with legs worn away
long ago and rotten bedding, and an old wardrobe, full of holes like a sieve,
make up the furniture.
name: A Once Cosy Bedroom

desc:
Shadows now dwell in what once was a bustling living hall. Wrapped in a deep
darkness, an old hearth seems asleep, as if recalling ancient and innumerable
stories, songs, and gossip, that certainly filled this room when hobbits still
lived in Soakedfeet. One can still fancy the smell of the seed-cakes, or the
shrill wheeze of the teapot on the heavy oaken table that occupies the centre of
the room. The other furniture left with its owner, as well as the frills,
profuse judging by the numerous holes and stains on the walls, and with them
were gone the voices and tales, plunging the room into a deep silence.
name: A Dark and Silent Living Room

desc:
A one-finger-thick layer of grayish dust covers the ground of this small
entrance hall, crowding about the borders, right where the walls stand. In spite
of the prints of time, you can still distinguish their light yellow shade, and
of course the smooth round section, that melts with the ceiling. On the northern
wall, several marks reveal the positions that were once occupied by pictures,
and perhaps wall lights, and even a chest of drawers. Close to the door, a long
peg rack, darkened by the dust, still clings to the wall, and one can easily
picture a row of coloured hoods hanging from it. The well-excavated corridor
goes into the hill, but, to the south, it seems to open into a room.
name: A Dusty Entrance Hall

desc:
This short but carefully hollowed passage constitutes the hub of the hobbit
hole. Leading into the hill, a few rooms open along its sides, approaching the
hillsides in search of air and light. Its section is perfectly round, except, of
course, for the thoroughly even floor, now covered with a thick layer of dense,
grayish dust that gathers in piles, as if matted. The tunnel seems to come to an
end here, but, to the north, a wide hole leads into a shadowy room, while, on
the south, you can see a worn, green, oval-shaped door.
name: A Rounded Corridor

desc:
The very air of this tiny room seems old and heavy. It is rancid and thick after
years of stillness, and loaded with dust that scratches your throat and burns
your lungs as you breathe it. The room is in utter disorder: high stacks of
rusty tools and broken utensils, and heaps of old and useless junk intermingle
following no pattern. Agricultural implements, pots, and crockery all appear to
be in rather bad condition. Half-hidden among the rubbish at the foot of one of
the walls, a little hole, only a few inches wide, disappears into the rock, its
dark mouth wrapped in shadows.
name: A Small Closet

desc:
You are now in a small room with a lofted ceiling, that most probably follows
the surface of the hillside. Opposite the entrance, where the ceiling is lower
and more inclined, a half-rotten wooden shutter seems to have been closed for
centuries. Below it, the wall has been carved in the shape of a stone table,
with two holes for both a sink and a fireplace. The wall on the left seems
dotted in numerous rusty nails, from which one day surely hung all kind of
utensils and pots. On the contrary, a spacious larder opens to the right, inside
which the smell of food still appears to float in the air.
name: An Empty Kitchen

desc:
A great stone furnace, leaning on the rear wall, focuses the activity in this
modest bakery, flooding the atmosphere with the crackling of burning logs, and
the unmistakable smell of honey cakes. It is very hot inside, and perhaps
because of that the hovel has no doors, but two holes leading outside on the
northern and eastern walls. An ample table, whitened by the flour, completes the
furnishings, and all sorts of utensils line up on its board: from a rolling-pin,
to several moulds, and mainly a heavy hand mill. Huge grain sacks are gathered
beneath the table, and so are red earthenware pots of honey and many other
ingredients.
name: Freuf's Bakery

desc:
The last few cabins of this small village stand on both sides of this narrow
little street, whose ground is here dusty and uneven, with abundant potholes
where pools turn up as soon as it rains. A small closed hut stands out on the
east and the door's lock seems quite unusual. The smell of newly cooked buns
comes hovering from inside another building right across the alley, along with
an occasional whistled or hummed tune. A bit further southwards, the path fades
into the green plains.
name: The Southern End

desc:
A rocky cavern opens before you. Its uneven ground contrasts its high ceiling.
So much so, that you can guess, more than see, what lies behind the deep shadows
above your head. The rocks that form the cave are craggy, with sharpened
projections and twisted shapes, and even those with the smoother surfaces are
dangerously slippery because of the moisture. This makes it necessary to advance
more slowly, even testing your footing to avoid falling. But, as if unaware of
the world outside, the atmosphere remains cold, though bearable, throughout the
whole year.
name: A Cold, Wet Grotto

desc:
This extensive porch, propped on wooden posts made of single tree-trunks, faces
south. Big, wooden, comfortable-looking benches allow you to sit and enjoy the
sight of the gardens, especially under the warmth of the westering sun, when the
last golden rays fall slanting on the flowers. A few broad steps descend into
the garden, where a small path seems to detour the house on its western flank,
and then it heads northwards.
name: A Veranda by the Gardens

desc:
This room is rather large but completely cramped with crates, sacks and loose
supplies, ranging from materials for the smith's work to items for everyday use.
Everything is ordered nicely and every crate or item seems to have its place.
Near the southern window lie a lot of tools and items that obviously are used to
fix worn out cloths, leathers, and other tools next to a cushion.
name: A Cramped Storage

desc:
Between grassy plains the Old Forest Road, covered with tracks of heavy carts,
runs from east to west. A muddy path, to which most fresh tracks lead, runs
south into the open plains. To the northwest a settlement, protected by dense
trees and a wooden wall, dominates the view. A stone, engraved with some
markings, has been placed at the junction of the path and road.
name: Junction in the Old Forest Road

desc:
Due to centuries of travel the road has been worn out, now forming a hollow way
between the plains. The road itself is partly overgrown, but some imprints of
hoofs are still present. The steep banks bordering it are covered in weeds and
small flowers, with here and there a small hole in them. Further away the flat
plains are covered with grasses and small shrubs.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The old hollow road runs through vast grasslands, and is itself partly overgrown
with grasses and weeds. Stones, which used to border the road, are barely
visible between tussocks of grass and piled up dirt. In the grasslands
surrounding the road, some solitary trees and low bushes grow here and there.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The grasslands are covered with a thick vegetation of typical grassland plants,
like clover, white daisies, purple thistle and yellow dandelion. Some grey
stones, mostly covered with yellow lichen, placed in a circular pattern form a
relic of an ancient civilisation. To the north of those stones a depression
splits the plains into two parts.
name: Grassy Plains

desc:
The grass grows high on the dark black soil, leaving no space for clover or any
other weeds. A few large grey stones covered with lichen dot the grassland. In
the shade of one of these stones small mushrooms grow on the fertile soil. To
the north a road, lying lower than the surrounding plains, runs from east to
west, while to the west a trail leads to the south.
name: Plains

desc:
This trail, covered with fresh tracks of cartwheels, is bordered by some large
willow trees and rotten logs of former trees. A small spring, dotted with animal
tracks, makes the path muddy, but also provides water to the trees and the
surrounding grassland. The trail splits off a larger road in the north and
continues its way to the south.
name: Old Trail

desc:
The ground is invisible because of the thick layer of vegetation. Grass covers
most of the plains, except where young trees and low bushes have taken over its
role. Some unnatural ditches divide the plains into regular sections. Water has
collected into each of the even ditches giving reeds and other wetland plants a
suitable habitat.
name: Overgrown Fields

desc:
Lush grass and large bushes cover the fertile ground of these plains. A few
scattered trees dot the landscape, the shade from their leaves providing some
protection from the elements to the creatures that live in the area. Signs of
small fauna can be seen across the landscape, the most obvious being an animal
trail leading south toward a copse of birch trees.
name: Fertile Plains

desc:
Close to the path in the west the remains of a camp fire can be seen; a circle
of grey stones surround a patch of burned earth. Around the stones the grasses
covering the plains have been pressed down by something large. A few skeletons
of deer, with knife marks all over them, lie scattered around those flattened
spaces.
name: Abandoned Camp

desc:
The trail, consisting of bare soil with small pebbles, is replaced by rich
grasslands to the east. In this area a dark patch, probably created by a fire,
is visible. Just west of the trail a haystack with a long wooden pole in the
middle has been made by the local people. Beyond the haystack cultivated fields
dominate the view.
name: Old Trail

desc:
The trail curves from north to west through the rich fields before leading to a
small village. Fresh tracks of carts and some droppings at the edge of the trail
indicate recent humanoid use. At the edge of the trail the vestiges of a cart,
wheels broken and the planks rotten, is partly hidden by the vegetation. At the
southern border regular stacked willow branches form a few tall piles.
name: Bend in an Old Trail

desc:
Grasses and other vegetation grow abundantly on the rich soil. The local birds
build their nests in the few solitary trees growing in this area, while animal
tracks leading from small holes beneath the trunks of those trees. The plains
extend to all directions except to the west where they are bordered by a trail.
name: Rich Plains

desc:
The Old Forest Road runs through a vast, grassy plain. The broad and well-built
road must have been actively used in the past, but is nowadays partly overgrown
with the wilderness, making the road look somewhat decayed and almost abandoned.
At the outer edge of the road, a steady row of low bushes follow it with an
occasional tree growing here and there among the bushes.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The surface of the low grassland is mainly coloured in different shades of light
brown, but green and yellow are also well represented. Half buried in the dry
grass, an animal skeleton is visible. A row of old fence poles sticks in a
straight row between the road and the plain. Farther away at the plain, there
are a few isolated clumps of yew trees with lowgreen bushes growing around them.
name: Low Grasslands

desc:
The grass grows in abundance in this field. The vast plain is filled with
grasses and various kinds of flowers. Around them, bees and other insects hover
in search of nectar. The rich vegetation makes these fields a pleasant habitat
for herbivores as well; fresh deer and rabbit tracks wander aimlessly throughout
the area. South of this sea of life, an old road can be spotted.
name: Grasslands

desc:
The wide grassland is covered with high grasses and lush, dense bushes. The
ground looks quite tangled and messy due to all the wild vegetation. At some
areas, several acres are covered by dark green bushes, while elsewhere it is
fully covered by plants with hollow stems and parallel-veined leaves. Throughout
the plains a few small tree saplings grow.
name: Near the Cleared Forest

desc:
A long time ago, large trees, most notably oaks and beeches, dwelt here. Now
only large stumps spanning more than five feet high remain. Ferns and mosses
grow between the roots of the trunks, among the occasional holes made by small
animals, that can be spotted on the ground. The gaps between the stumps are
inhabited by young willow trees and bramble bushes.
name: Cleared Forest

desc:
The Old Forest Road bends around a small rise to the north-east. A few old cart
tracks imprinted in the dry mud form the surface of the road. At the southern
boundary of the road, rocks and stones of all sizes have carefully been aligned
with each other to prevent the erosion of the road in the case of heavy rains.
Thin grass tufts grow from the cracks of the stones.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
This clear stretch of the Old Forest Road runs directly from the east to the
west. The sparse vegetation close to the road, in combination with the thick
bushes further away show that the road has been wider in the past. To the north
flat plains can be seen, whilst to the south a thick thorny hedge planted on top
of a low dike blocks all passage.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The Old Forest Road runs from the east to the west. In most places, the surface
of the road is hard and dusty. In the middle of the road, faint traces of
cartwheels can be spotted among the other bumps and holes of the road, while at
the edges, grasses and clovers are in the process of retaking the road. On the
south side of the road, a low dike covered with bushes blocks the view.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The sandy, light brown road makes a long, steady curve, as it winds from the
west to the south. The road is several yards in width, allowing even two wagons
to easily pass each other. There are low, grassy trenches on either side of the
road. Behind those, the ground elevates quickly a few yards, giving the
impression of travelling in a dry riverbed. Thick trees grow on the eastern side
of the road, making both the travel and visibility very limited.
name: Winding Old Forest Road

desc:
These fields have clearly been used for farming in the past, but since then they
have become quite feral. The ground, partly covered with young bushes and high
grass, is uneven. Several long rows of bumpy furrows are still visible within
the undergrowth. To the north, the fields are bordering the Old Forest Road.
Apart from that, the flat fields continue on in all directions.
name: Abandoned Fields

desc:
The field is covered with different types of vegetation. A short yellowish
grass, with several shades of brown and green, fills the ground. Low bushes and
occasional flower clumps grow here and there. Few beech trees stand above the
other foliage, giving some protection from the sun. Open plains seem to continue
in every direction, although to the south the ground begins to slope.
name: Wild Fields

desc:
Several square-shaped open areas have been cleared on the otherwise bushy
plains. Squares look cultivated, and are growing vegetables and other plants.
Regularly used grassy paths surround the fields. At the lower places a faint
smell of excrement, possibly manure, comes from the ground. At the end of the
fields are piles of leaves and rotten vegetables. A long, trimmed hedge
surrounds a small farm area located to the east.
name: Farmed Fields

desc:
This field is covered with beets. They have green leaves with red veins, and in
many cases the top part of the red root has been transformed to a slight green
by the light of the sun. At the northern end of the field, a broad dike covered
with dense bushes protects the fields from cold winds and from the unwanted
trespassers travelling the Old Forest Road.
name: Field covered with Beets

desc:
A narrow trail separates from the dusty path, leading into the front yard of a
farmhouse made of thick, wooden planks. The outside of this house was once
painted in bright red and orange, but due to the sun's bleaching, the colours
have faded into a shade of light brown, with the exception of right below the
roof where the original splendour is still visible. A long, thick hedge
circulates the fields behind the house.
name: Bend in the Dusty Path

desc:
A major part of this farmed soil has been planted with potatoes, which are
growing well with green leaves and white flowers. Everywhere else, rotten
potatoes can be seen breaking out of the soil, ravaged by critters. A tall dike,
topped by several thick bushes, blocks the passage to the north and east. A
small natural passage has formed through the wall to the north, due to erosion.
name: Potato Fields

desc:
The Old Forest Road is covered with dirt and short grass. It curves around a
small hill located north-east of the road. The hill is mainly covered with low
bushes and a few solitary tree that rise into the sky. On the west side of the
road, the passage is blocked by a long dike covered with bramble bushes. In the
south, a dirt path lined with trees leads to some buildings.
name: Winding Old Forest Road

desc:
A grassy, green path runs through the winding fields, connecting the Old Forest
Road from the north to a small farm located in the west. A neat line of beech
and ash trees has been planted on both sides of the path at regular intervals.
The slender and delicate trees are about four or five feet tall.
name: Grassy Path

desc:
The road is covered with loose sand, with an occasional small tussock here and
there. It is hard to distinguish the boundary between the road and the
surrounding plains, because the grass gradually increases in height and in
density. The northern edge of the road is interrupted by a small path running
north towards a hut. To the east, the border of the forest consisting of huge
trees can be seen.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
A low roofed hut stands at the forest border. There is a modest yard around the
house, surrounded by a rough, bright yellow plank fence. Huge piles of wood have
been placed between the nearest trunks of the forest. A thicket of dense
branched trees and messy underbrush starts behind the fence. A small path starts
from the garden gate and forks, where the path to the south joins the Old Forest
Road opposite the eastern path leads into a dark forest.
name: Small Path by the Forest Border

desc:
The walls and the floor of this small hut have been constructed of thick wooden
beams, while the roof is roughly built of planks and bricks. There is a small
window next to the entrance, giving a view to the garden outside. Axes, saws and
wedges hang from nails on the wall, along with some worn working clothes. Close
to the back wall, a cupboard divides the hut in such a way that a confined space
containing a bed has been created to the far end of the room.
name: Lumberjack's Hut

desc:
A worn out path leads through the dim forest, winding slowly between the trees
and bushes. Someone has been chopping a lot of trees down recently, as stumps,
cut branches, and other trash from the fallen trees litter the forest; even a
few small clearings have been formed next to the path. Outside the cleared parts
the tall, shady trees are covered with hanging vines and other entangled
vegetation. The forest looks dark and dangerous.
name: Forest Path

desc:
The shady forest is dark and extremely threatening. It is unknown how high the
ancient trees reach, as the unbroken net of vines, leaves, and branches form the
ceiling a few yards above the ground. Nothing seems to be moving anywhere, even
the air is totally still. This place has a strong malignant aura; it is as if
the gloomy forest was alive and an ancient evilness was creeping behind every
bush and tree.
name: Murky Forest

desc:
Huge, bumpy trees grow here, forming impenetrable clumps in the dense forest.
The colour of the trunks varies between green, brown, and black among the
occasional fungi that grows upon some trunks. There is quite a lot of
miscellaneous ground-level foliage, but not so much that it would block the
passage. The uppermost branches tangle together forming an almost impenetrable
canopy.
name: Dense Forest

desc:
The eastern edge of the forest is filled with young, vital trees, thriving
clusters of thorn bushes, and small, open areas within the forest, where the
mushrooms and ferns grow. Looking deeper into the woods, the trees are
significantly taller and thicker, and the vegetation gets quickly denser. Here
and there are closely set copses, where brambles grow around the thick tree
formations.
name: Border of the Forest

desc:
There is a wide, flat clearing occupying the area. It grows hay, low bushes and
other undergrowth allowing clear visibility into all directions. The surrounding
trees slowly continue their attempts to reclaim the earth, having began their
journey many years ago. Someday the looming forest walls on both sides will meet
here again, as they did in the ancient times when Mirkwood was still known as
Greenwood the Great and the shadow had not fallen on the peaceful forest.
name: Wide Clearing

desc:
The spacious barn looks very clean, as if someone has been taking excellent care
of it. All of the supplies and items are in good condition and well- organised.
The walls of the barn are made of broad planks and slightly spaced apart to let
the fresh air circulate freely from the outside. At one end of the barn there
are large doors leading out; and at the other, a small door leading to the
living quarters. A huge haystack towers in the corner of the barn, and a small,
blue cart stands next to it. The other side of the barn is filled with animal
stalls.
name: Well-kept Barn

desc:
The farmhouse has been split into two parts. One part is filled with crates full
of carrots, potatoes and other vegetables. Next to them, a neat collection of
various gardening tools has been arranged on the back wall. The other part of
the house, separated partly by a wall and partly by curtains, contains a stove,
with a kettle on it, and other furniture usually found in small homes.
name: Wooden Farmhouse

desc:
Dense vegetation covers the soil, among the faint remains of the low irrigation
ditches that mark the presence of former agricultural developments. Near one of
these ditches, a small, ruined shelter, the kind that usually was built for
livestock, has been built between the bushes. The shelter consists of a few
rocks, planks, and poles, and has now been overgrown with nettles and brambles.
name: Bushy Plains near the Road

desc:
The Old Forest Road runs along the tree line, following the curves of the gloomy
forest, located on the north side of the road. The surface of the road is rough;
sometimes there are medium sized stones; sometimes there are deep ruts in the
road. On the border of the forest, large trees and the messy undergrowth have
grown so tightly next to each other that it is nearly impossible to enter the
forest. On the south side of the road lie vast, feral plains.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The outskirts of the northern forest frame the road. In general, the road is in
proper condition, although occasional grass tufts and even small bushes grow
here and there on it. Based on the condition of the road, it is evident that
only few, if any, travellers frequent the road nowadays. The surrounding terrain
is not particularly harsh, and one could travel easily in any direction from
here.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
The tall trees suddenly part into a forest clearing, where weeds and some small
bushes grow. Winding between the trees, a small forest trail meets another path
in the clearing where an odd looking stone, covered with green and grey moss,
stands at the crossing. The forest opens up to the south, while in other
directions it gets denser.
name: Small Forest Glade

desc:
The grassy plain is almost like a canyon between the two forest walls, which are
standing at the both ends of the open area. Although the dark forest to the west
is big and truly majestic, it is still nothing compared to the endless Mirkwood,
which extends into unknown distances in the eastern horizon. The Old Forest Road
runs to the south.
name: Fields by the Forest Wall

desc:
The forest has suffered a bitter loss here, as if someone has been cutting trees
down throughout the area. In the middle of a small opening, an especially
enormous tree has fallen and only a gigantic stump remains where it once stood.
The stump has a strong, thick bark which is covered with fungi. However, the
upper part of the stump is clear, showing hundreds and hundreds of growth rings.
name: A Giant Stump

desc:
Low undergrowth fills the plains, allowing excellent visibility in all
directions. The only exceptions to this pattern are the lonely bushes and
occasional larger rocks that rise upwards from the ground. Here and there,
animal tracks run back and forth on the ground. To the north, the Old Forest
Road is located between the plains and the forest. In other directions, the
lonesome expanse of plains can be seen.
name: Plains by the Road

desc:
The northern edge of the wide scrubland is covered with a myriad of plants, such
as tall grasses and scraggely bushes. The ground is sloping slightly and there
is no sign of any kind of organised agriculture. The open scrubland stretches
onwards to the south and west, with the exception to the east, where the terrain
transfers into a long, abruptly-rising slope filled with thickets.
name: Sloping Plains

desc:
The road runs through a desolated landscape. The terrain is rather forested,
trees and bushes of various types grow all around the road, especially large
black beeches grow here in abundance. North of the road, the wilderness looks
impenetrable, whereas the southern region is mainly covered by bushes and is
easy to travel. To the east, the mighty Mirkwood is quite close.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
A broad zone of bushes spreads between the plains and the great forest of
Mirkwood. The bushes are so high and so filled with branches that they do not
permit a clear line of sight; resulting in a confusing warren of vegetation
where it is easy to get lost. To the west, there is a bush filled slope with so
steep an inclination that it is impossible to go there at all.
name: Rambling Bushes

desc:
The terrain is very challenging inside the dense thicket. Neither clear path nor
any kind of wider open area exists, which would make the smooth travelling in
this green shrubbery possible. Behind every bush there seems to be just another
copse waiting. It is difficult to keep track of directions here.
name: Tangled Bushes

desc:
Lush, green grass covers these plains for as far as the eye can see. The plains
continue south and eastward, seemingly without end. Many miles to the west, even
the most inexperienced traveller could spot the smoke and, if the wind was
favourable, smell the telltale signs of a village.
name: Vast Grasslands

desc:
The massive plains, so characteristic of the lands surrounding the Anduin River
far to the west, end abruptly here at a small grove of trees. As large and
unyielding as these plains appear to be, they are not so mighty as to withstand
the domination of man. Just to the west, a small man-made grove of elms stand as
cover for a large village just beyond.
name: End of the Grasslands

desc:
Though not as impressive as the walls surrounding some towns, the walls of this
village appear impossible to penetrate. On close inspection, it becomes clear
that these walls are not solid but live vines and brush intertwining live elm
trees. The brush has been woven so tightly that no light from inside the village
escapes.
name: Outside the Village Walls

desc:
Massive trees and dark, dense vegetation border the age-old, sandy road running
through the forest. The road was originally several yards wide, but since then
the forest has overwhelmed it in several places, and only a narrow trail
remains. A tangled mess of leaves, ferns and branches grows around and above the
road forming a thick cover of vegetation and absorbing most of the light and
sounds to itself which creates an echoless and oppressive atmosphere.
name: Old Forest Trail

desc:
This is the place where the Old Forest Road meets the border of Mirkwood. The
huge, gloomy forest wall seems to continue endlessly, as ancient and malevolent
looking trees fulfil the view by towering into great heights. The edge of
Mirkwood is intact, save for a place where an arching tunnel mouth looms between
two massive, leaning tree trunks. An old, worn sign stands by the road, and
behind it the road disappears into the dark, silent foliage. Only a short way
into the forest an old tree has fallen recently and blocks the path with its
entangled crown.
name: The Entrance to Mirkwood

desc:
A trail of densely packed soil covered with gravel makes its way through high
grass and bushes. Roots break the carefully laid-out path from time to time. The
forest looms over the trail, with beech and oak growing very dense both in the
north and south. Darkness engulfs Mirkwood in all directions save to the east
and west, where the fictive safety of the trail continues.
name: Old Forest Trail

desc:
Some parts of the forest have been cleared of their once majestic trees. An old
trail makes its way through Mirkwood. Old stumps alongside the road are covered
in old, grey moss, and others infested with malicious fungi and pests. The
forest itself lies dense, but traversable, to the north. In the south it once
again grows tall, and the trees stand close, denying any possible way for
further exploring. The trail continues its slithering route through the heavy
undergrowth in the east and west.
name: Old Forest Trail

desc:
Stumps and roots interrupt the weather-beaten old trail, which was made by
pebbles and gravel being laid over densely packed black soil. The trail has no
defining borders, simply merging into the young trees of the forest on either
side. The woods grow unfriendly and twisted to the south, leaving only a small
passage available for further travel. To the north the trees grow in dense
lines, looming in a threatening manner over the pathway. The trail itself
continues its way through Mirkwood to the east and west.
name: Old Forest Trail

desc:
The trail rises a few feet here, having been built on a mound of dirt, as it
makes its way through the stout, tall trees. The terrain is relatively
undamaged. The few huge branches and tree trunks which have fallen lie covered
in vines, moss and various other plants. The menacing oak and beech lean over
the trail, shutting out the natural light efficiently with their crowns. The old
forest trail extends its arms to the east and west.
name: Old Forest Trail

desc:
Fallen branches and twigs lie scattered across the trail. Small pebbles and
decomposing vegetation lie in small mounds, serving as homes for various
insects. Tree stumps, covered by fungi and moss, lie dead alongside the pathway.
Low, forested hills rise tall in the south, engulfed in a dark, menacing gloom.
The trail itself continues its path to the east and west.
name: Old Forest Trail

desc:
Zigzagging its way through the grass which stands several feet tall, the trail
cannot avoid the disrupting power of ancient roots. Decayed shrubs and fallen
trees line the trail. The threat of the forest is ever present, with its oak,
beech and fir uneasily following every move of possible intruders. The trail
marches on to the east and west.
name: Old Forest Trail

desc:
Mirkwood grows dense in the north, completely engulfed in darkness. The forest
is murky and its vegetation leaves little space for exploration. Weathered and
old, this road slithers through stumps and tall grass to the east and west. At
the feet of a great oak a bear's den has been pillaged and destroyed.
name: Old Forest Road

desc:
A dense network of old trees blocks out the sky with their great crowns. The
majority of the darkened trees are covered by a damp, grey moss, which seems to
make the air even more humid. Many trees have fallen and lie rotting on the
ground to the south, creating a passageway to an old trail. The forest grows
close to the north and east.
name: Mirkwood Forest

desc:
The trees stand tall and dense, their majestic crowns block out any possible
natural light. Fungi and a variety of mosses cover the fallen as well as
standing flora, leaving many of the trunks and branches in a brittle state. The
forest is growing thicker in all directions, leaving only a narrow passage to
the south.
name: Mirkwood Forest

desc:
Great oaks reach towards the sky, leaning their great crowns against one
another, supporting each other's heavy weight. Together they create a natural
blanket blocking most outside light. The undergrowth is extremely dense in the
south, forming an impenetrable wall of vegetation. To the north Mirkwood opens
up slightly, sloping down towards a trail. It seems possible to travel through
the murky vegetation lying to the east.
name: Murky Forest

desc:
The skeleton of Mirkwood is slowly starting to wane. Old, rotten trees have
fallen to the ground, piling up in the east to form an impermeable wall. This
pile of decomposing vegetable matter has turned into a haven for cockroaches,
termites and various deteriorating fungi. Dense, heavy forest grows in the north
and west, while in the south a trail runs on its way through the woods.
name: Mirkwood Forest

desc:
Poison ivy reaches out from the trees, entangling fallen trees and decomposed
bushes. The stifling humidity makes the already foul air even harder to bear.
Some thick vines and roots have been cleared away to the east, leaving a small
trail which appears to lead between the bases of the trees. Darkened trunks
block any vision to the north and south, leaving weary travellers with just two
options for further exploration: down the slope eastwards, or deeper into the
dark forest in the west.
name: Deep inside Mirkwood

desc:
The sloping forest falls in from the west, with its trees poised over a myriad
of bushes, branches and other fallen vegetation. The ground is covered in a
dense mishmash of vines and shrubs. Roots and ivy create a natural roof, keeping
out most of the natural light. The shadowed forest continues to rise above you
in the south, while in the east it settles slightly. The view to the north is
completely blocked by the heavy vegetation.
name: Deep inside Mirkwood

desc:
Great vines and roots have taken over here, leaving the trees in despair.
Leaning towards each other they form a close-to-regular, knitted pattern,
shielding the lower forest from any outside light. An old animal's den has been
completely ruined by the abundant vegetation. The boulders and rocks by the
entrance seem to have frozen in time, forever stuck among the twisted roots. The
forest ivy climbs several feet up into the air towards the west, creating a
brittle roof.
name: Among the Roots

desc:
Poison ivy descends the trunks of the surrounding trees, together with roots and
decomposed trees creating a very cumbersome environment to explore. Similar
growth can be seen in the north. In the west the tangles reach for each other,
ensnaring each others' stems in midair, forming an impenetrable quilt. Like a
fortress wall, Mirkwood rises tall and strong to the south.
name: Among the Roots

desc:
Enormous roots of black oak trees rise high above the ground creating an
intimidating, tight meshwork, rendering the area extremely difficult to
traverse. A change in the structure of vegetation can be noticed to the east and
north, where vines and ivy seem to seek the forest floor. A steep, overgrown
slope blocks any further travel to the west while the imposing vegetation to the
south doesn't leave any obvious route to move forward.
name: Underneath the Forest

desc:
The great oaks and beech stand tall and proud, their leaves, branches and twigs
mingling together in a single mass like a patchwork quilt far up in the air.
Roots and vines entangle each other on the ground, as though refusing to reveal
any easy way to walk here. Great bushes move uneasily in the north, blocking out
any further view in that direction. The whole forest is engulfed in a sombre
darkness.
name: Mirkwood Forest

desc:
Vines and roots create a forest floor shaped like a pit filled with serpents.
Shadows of branches, trunks and roots form a complex pattern on the ground. Ivy
is hanging down from the tops of the fir and oak, making this area fairly
demanding to explore. A slight uphill slope in the east leads from this
entangled area into a gloomy forest. Heavily forested hills rise in the south.
The vicious underbrush broadens its space to the north, creating a natural
tunnel, deep underneath the trees.
name: Among the Roots

desc:
The vicious-looking trees lean in to one another, guarding each other's backs
from intruders. Mirkwood stands twisted and tall, engulfing the vegetation in an
immaculate veil of darkness. The beech and oak leave a passage open to the east
and south, ensnaring the heavy underbrush with their roots and vines.
name: A Shaded Forest

desc:
Gnarled branches have fallen to the ground, left dehydrated and brittle by an
old fire. A few majestic trees still stand strong, with their crowns reaching
for the sky, and their trunks forever marked with burns and deep cuts.
Vine-entangled roots rise from the murky soil, offering new foundations for ivy
and periwinkle. In the north Mirkwood lies engulfed in shadow while in the west
it bears the marks of long-forgotten fires. Far below, down an uneven slope, an
old forest trail can be discerned to the south.
name: A Shaded Forest

desc:
Great branches from the ancient trees lie spread across the forest floor, broken
under the twisted, scorched tree trunks. Stout young birch and fir have already
grown dense since the fire, and are already well on the way to restoring the
darkness of Mirkwood. The forest with its young trees expands into the east and
north. A steep hillside leads further west into a more heavily-wooded part of
Mirkwood.
name: A Scorched Forest

desc:
Trees, scorched to their core, have fallen heavily to the ground. However, the
still standing giants of the forest, despite their gaping wounds and obvious
marks of fire, still manage to embrace the area in darkness. Light vegetation
has slowly started to take over from the incinerated trees. The disfigured
forest expands far into the south, while in the east a tall mound of rocks and
boulders appears to have protected the remaining forest from the fire.
name: A Scorched Forest

desc:
The air is dark, heavy and thick under the malevolent trees, which seem to lean
towards travellers, stretching out to reach them. The movement is difficult
because of the giant roots and branches that are intertwined everywhere with
each other. And where the nature has not blocked the way, sticky, silvery spider
webs have been woven between the trunks.
name: Dark Forest

desc:
The forest here is marked by a meshwork of twisting vines, interweaving the
alive with the dead. The dense vegetation creates tall natural walls,
purposefully encircling anyone trying to explore it. The trees loom over one
another, stopping the sun and stars from casting their light into Mirkwood.
name: Deep inside Mirkwood

desc:
The darkness surrounds, even engulfs this area. The solid canopy of the forest
hangs above with heavy branches growing downwards as other free directions do
not exist. So thick is the ceiling made of wood and leaves that daylight
probably never shines on this feral place. Some stones lie on the ground; their
edges half concealed by moss and ferns creating treacherous places to stumble
upon. A deathlike silence pervades the whole forest.
name: Dark, Oppressive Forest

desc:
The forest does not look healthy here. Some of the big trees are clearly rotten,
and they look like they may fall down at any moment. A few trees have broken and
collapsed already, lying among the vegetation as a part of the decayed, smelly
mess that covers the ground. Above, the upper part of branches have grown
compactly together, making the forest very dark.
name: Rotten Forest by the Road

desc:
Grand oaks and beech create a shadowy forest, rising from a brittle, dry ground.
The great roots and vines have sucked the life out of the earthy forest floor. A
great bird's nest has fallen to the ground, broken up by pests and putrid fungi.
The dense vegetation, combined with the presence of death, bury Mirkwood in a
sombre darkness. The dark forest lies explorable to the south, west and east.
name: Murky Forest

desc:
Under and between the black roots, a narrow tunnel snakes its way in the
darkness. The surrounding roots are thick and gnarled, seemingly penetrating
deeper and deeper to the ground to suck any life force there still may be. The
black soil around the roots is humid and rather cold. The tunnel ends to a dead
end to the west, and leads forward to the east.
name: Dead End in the Darkness

desc:
The ground is very uneven here and old, decomposed trees are incorporated into
the heavy undergrowth. The ancient trees rise tall and dark. It appears
difficult to travel further east, up over a small rise, due to the heavily
entangled roots and boughs. Parts of the forest here have been heavily ravaged,
their trunks gaping with open wounds. Animal trails lead into the heavy
undergrowth to the south, while to the west a faint gloom spreads across the
forested hills.
name: A Ravaged Forest

desc:
Malicious-looking periwinkle reaches downwards from withered oak and ash,
intertwining with the foliage and stretching far across the smothering terrain.
A dense canopy hangs far up in the air, efficiently preventing most natural
light from penetrating. Mouldy vines and roots spread over the forest floor.
Fallen beeches serve well as homes for various parasites. The darkness which is
Mirkwood may be further explored to the east and south.
name: Eerie Forest

desc:
A pitch black, dead silent maze makes it way through the heavy vegetation. It is
supported by the roots of the great forest above, intertwined by poison ivy and
vines. Mirkwood appear to shift, slowly but constantly. There are no obvious
landmarks to orient onself with, and the area is limited for further
exploration.
name: Underneath the Forest

desc:
Mirkwood grows less dense here, yet the crowns of the trees manage to keep the
darkness consistent, while a heavy moisture seems to weigh down the lukewarm
air. Various forms of underbrush grow on the forest floor, intertwined with
poison ivy. The ivy appears to nurture itself from the beech and fir on which it
climbs. The forest opens up towards an old trail in the north, and to a
malicious pit of roots and vines in the west.
name: Low Hills of Mirkwood

desc:
Deep within the infinity of this enormous sea of grass, like a tiny vessel
drifting in the roaring ocean, you are at the mercy of the great surges of grass
raised by the wind. When it blows, the whole mass of grass bends to and fro, and
huge green waves run all through the grassland, the high blades swinging
regularly, and the noise of their incessant rubbing, along with the shriek of
the wind, contributing to the stormy atmosphere.
name: In the Sea of Grass

desc:
A small and simple stall with a neat look stands to the west. The smell of fresh
hay, and some occasional loud yet mild neighs reach you from behind its coarse
gate, where, half-hidden in shadows, you glimpse heaps of golden yellow straw. A
little path, that comes running through wide gardens from the southern end of
the house, approaches near here before bending eastwards, to the encounter of
the main one that leads into the courtyard.
name: In Front of a Barn

desc:
Deep within the infinity of this enormous sea of grass, like a tiny vessel
drifting in the roaring ocean, you are at the mercy of the great surges of grass
raised by the wind. When it blows, the whole mass of grass bends to and fro, and
huge green waves run all through the grassland, the high blades swinging
regularly, and the noise of their incessant rubbing, along with the shriek of
the wind, contributing to the stormy atmosphere.
name: In the Sea of Grass
